basis: Independent audiovisual model observation, not human listening or production approval

original_result.comparison_reason: First delivers a technically sound, coherent, and precisely staged schematic explanation of the data center cooling pilot. Its state changes (temperature gradient rising in the first unit, resetting upon repair, and intermittent spiking in the second unit) are clearly visualized on the cooling apparatus itself, supported by purposeful movements of the autonomous inspection robot and staged handheld tool. In contrast, Second suffers from a severe compositing mask glitch at 07.0s (a jagged white tear and floating detached fan asset during the transition into the robot close-up), along with disconnected floating props (a wrench floating over the exterior wire fan grille without mechanical contact, and oversized floating checklist clipboards) that weaken physical contact and causal consequence.

first.one_viewing_summary: A clean, disciplined 3D schematic model tracks the Houston data center pilot, illustrating thermal differentials, robotic inspection, handheld verification, condenser repair, and intermittent spikes with meticulous disclosure labels.
observed_strengths: Direct causal visualization: cooling coils clearly illuminate coral to show heat accumulation, clear to teal upon repair, and flash to represent intermittent spikes.
The inspection robot and handheld console carts have clear spatial grounding, purposeful trajectories, and well-motivated tracking camera moves.

Thorough and honest attribution overlays ('Schematic temperature comparison', 'Illustration. Vendor-reported pilot', 'Other unit • fault unconfirmed') enforce strict source hygiene without overclaiming.

defects.observed: The opening frame and initial 3.5 seconds feature a static wide schematic view where only the lower coil bar slowly fills, offering modest scroll-stopping visual energy before the robot arrives.
The final pilot-ongoing scene holds a static arrangement of the units, cart, and robot for over 9 seconds with subtle fan rotations as the only motion.

second.one_viewing_summary: A stylized 2.5D illustrated treatment using illustrated cutout sprites and character props, undermined by a broken wipe transition at 07.0s and floating non-contact props.
observed_strengths: Expressive, appealing hero sprite design for the mobile robot and warm condenser unit.
Strong initial hook composition with rising thermal distortion lines and clear bold headline typography.

defects.observed: At 07.0s during the transition to the medium shot, an unrendered white polygon mask tears across the center of the frame, showing clipped machinery fragments and a floating disembodied fan wheel before the shot resolves.
The gloved technician hand holding a wrench simply floats and bobs in front of the protective wire fan mesh rather than engaging any bolt, fitting, or condenser component.
Oversized, generic 2D clipboard clip-art cards pop into the scene without spatial integration or grounding in the environment.

original_result.audio_observed: Both candidates share identical, well-balanced sound design: authoritative, natural voiceover narration synchronized with subtle mechanical fan ambient hums, soft electronic verification cues, and Kevin MacLeod's 'Deep Haze' score properly mixed under dialogue without masking.
original_result.source_limits: Both films properly disclose vendor self-reporting from FacilityOps AI, maintain that the pilot is ongoing as of the September 23 update, clarify that the second unit's temperature spike is unconfirmed as a fault, and avoid claiming autonomous robotic repair.
